newsitem.title: RWANDA: Canadian-led Zaire force ordered to close down.
newsitem.headline: Canadian-led Zaire force ordered to close down.

text.p: Canadian units in a multinational force for eastern Zaire were ordered on Saturday to close down and pull out of Rwanda and their main base in Uganda, a Canadian army spokesman said.

"I understand a decision was taken in New York formally closing out the mission. With that decision we are pulling out of Kigali in the next few days and Kampala will send its people back to Canada over the next few weeks," said Major Rob Babiuk, a spokesman for the force's Canadian liaison team in Rwanda.
"We received word this morning from New York and are packing up," said Babiuk. "We have 19 people here and everyone will be gone by noon tomorrow except for four of us to tie things up."
The Canadian liaison team arrived in Rwanda on November 17 when the international community was pushing for a multinational force to intervene in eastern Zaire to help aid fleeing Rwandan refugees.

The force, under the command of Lieutenant-General Maurice Baril, has its headquarters in the Ugandan capital Kampala but has been unable to do much more than coordinate data from aerial searches for refugees and prepare some plans for aid airdrops.

"General Baril will come down to Kigali early next week to pay a courtesy call on the government and then we will be out of Rwanda entirely," said Babiuk, adding he believed headquarters in Kampala was also in the process of packing up and leaving.
